comment: Two reviewers on one corpus, one judge, one ground truth - the first comparison this project has that is not
a volume and not a recollection.
**And the result is a loss, stated first.** **A competitor scores F1 0.3784 and this repository's engine scores
0** - **on the same 50 labelled issues, judged by the same `deepseek-chat`, over the same pull requests.**
**And the competitor used this repository's own model.** **`OCR_LLM_URL` points at the same DeepSeek endpoint the
judge uses**, so **the gap is not a model difference** - **it is a difference in what each system does with the
**And both numbers carry the balance they were drawn on**, because **five earlier runs of this same job produced
F1 values between 0 and 0.1724 on this corpus with insufficient credit on some of them.**
rootCauseNotes: **the engine emitted 2 findings across 5 pull requests and matched none of 50** - so the gap is not ranking, it is emission: the competitor produced 24 candidates and this engine produced 2
**the same model produced both sets**, so the difference is in how each system frames the task for it
**the competitor's findings carry a category and a severity and a suggested diff**; this project's carry a lane
**and the engine's recall on this corpus has never exceeded 0.10 across eight runs**, so this is not a draw that went badly - it is a ceiling
whatThisDoesNotSay: that the competitor's 10 false positives are wrong - that needs a second judge or a human, and this run has neither
that AACR-Bench is neutral - Alibaba built both the tool and the benchmark it wins on, and this comparison holds that constant rather than resolving it

why: **995 lanes attempted and 995 succeeded** - **no lane failed, and no file failed to load**, so **nothing was dropped.**
**Those 995 lanes produced one finding.** **So the engine read every file and declined to report**, which is **a different defect from a pipeline that loses findings.**
**And its precision is 1.0** - **the single finding it emitted matched a labelled issue.** **So it does not over-report; it under-reports to the point of silence.**
whatItRulesOut: **a lane handling defect** - there were no failures to handle
**an input defect on this run** - 199 files were split and reviewed, against 1 before the split
**a credit defect** - `creditExhausted` is false and the balance is recorded
whatItPointsAt: **not the finding cap**: the prompt records that the cap was raised to eight for one run and put back, because **the raise recovered one true positive and halved precision**, so **the cap is not what sets the candidate count.**

**the lane granularity**: **995 lanes over 199 files is five per file**, and **each lane sees one file in isolation** - so **a defect that spans files is invisible to every lane that could report it**, and **the ground truth carries 2 Repo Level issues by construction.**
**the competitor reviews the whole pull request in one call**, which is **the difference between a view that can contain a cross-file defect and one that cannot.**

samples.note: **two draws, and both reviewers moved** - so a single comparison here is a sample rather than a number

shapeComparison.reading: **the competitor produces about twenty times the candidates at half the precision and wins F1 by eight** - so **precision is not this engine's constraint, it is at its maximum, and the deficits that remain are candidate count and view scope rather than ranking or filtering.**

wholePrArm.view: one call over the whole pull request diff

why: **The whole-PR arm replaced 995 per-file lanes with 25 whole-diff lanes** - **a forty-fold reduction in calls and the competitor's own view** - **and F1 moved from 0.0392 to 0.0385.**
**Both arms found exactly one true positive**, so **the change of view changed neither the recall nor the count of what was found.**
**And both arms use the same engine**, which produced one or two findings under either view - so **the constraint is in the emission mechanism rather than in what the mechanism is shown.**
**And the competitor, in the same run, found fourteen** - so **the difference is not the corpus, the judge, the model or the view**, all four of which are now held constant.
whatItLeaves: **the emission mechanism itself**: the prompt's selection rules, the finding schema, and whatever filters a lane's findings before they reach the counter.

clampFix.verdict: **the prediction was right, and both halves of it happened**
why: **The commit predicted**: if the 207 were real findings discarded for having file-relative line numbers, recall would move substantially; if they were noise, precision would fall while recall rose.
**Both happened**: **recall went from 0.02 to 0.56**, and **precision went from 1.0 to 0.061**. So **some were real - 27 new true positives - and most were noise - 431 false positives.**
**And F1 rose from 0.0392 to 0.11**, which is **the first movement in this figure that came from a fix rather than from a draw.**

**And the recall now exceeds the competitor's**: **0.56 against 0.3409.** **The remaining gap is precision** - **0.061 against 0.5357** - and **that is a different and more specific target than the one this iteration started with.**

precisionCurve.note: **a curve rather than a point**: each row is one run, and the knobs are the emission filter and the deduplication threshold. **F1 has now moved 5.2x from the pre-fix baseline, and every move has an explanation.**

rows.note: 207 of 208 discarded by the coordinate check
recall 28x; the duplicates were counted as separate findings
**its own spread across runs is 0.32 to 0.42**
**488 merged to 128**; precision 2.3x, and **ten true positives were merged away**
**22 fewer false positives and not one true positive lost** - so **the threshold was still too low at 0.6, and it has not yet cost anything at 0.8**

precisionCurve.reading: **The curve is now monotone in F1 and every step has a mechanism.** **And the last step showed over-merging, which is a threshold rather than a structural problem** - **the next iteration moves the 60% content-word threshold up and measures again.**

whatChanged.note: **87 percent of the false positives were duplicates**, so **the duplicate hypothesis was right**, and **the ten lost true positives are what the threshold costs**

thresholdCurve.reading: **F1 rises with the threshold and recall does not fall**, so **the merge was still over-inclusive at 0.6 and is not yet costing anything at 0.8**. **The next point is 0.9.**
why: **22 fewer false positives from 0.6 to 0.8, and exactly the same 18 true positives.**
**So the additional 22 were duplicates that a looser threshold had called distinct**, and **no genuinely different defect was protected by the looser threshold.**
**And that means the threshold has not yet reached the point where it starts costing recall** - which is **the point the curve is looking for.**
